historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (47.4% 3yr, 34.7% 5yr) is elevated due to low post-IPO book value base and GAAP losses masking retained earnings. FCF 5yr CAGR is meaningless (FY2020 base FCF of $12.5M is distorted). EPS CAGRs are not calculable due to persistent GAAP losses. FCF 3yr CAGR of 34.1% selected as primary growth rate anchor for a high-growth SaaS company, with near-term growth moderated to match ARR growth guidance (~21-22% for FY2026, ~20% for FY2027) and then decelerating toward terminal rate.

base.description: Steady post-outage recovery, 20-22% ARR growth sustained through FY2027-28, gradual deceleration as law of large numbers sets in. FCF margins improve modestly from ~27% toward ~30% as S&M leverage kicks in.

bull.description: Platform consolidation accelerates: CrowdStrike captures outsized share of enterprise security consolidation, Charlotte AI drives premium upsells, $10B ARR vision materializes faster. FCF margins expand to 30%+ as platform leverage drives operating efficiency.

bear.description: July 2024 trust deficit lingers, Microsoft competitive pressure intensifies, Delta litigation results in large settlement, ARR growth slows to low-teens. FCF margins compress as elevated S&M spend fails to reaccelerate growth.

sensitivity.note: Base scenario. Rows = WACC (8-12%), Columns = Terminal Growth (2-4%). Values are intrinsic value per share in USD.

probability_weighted.note: Probability-weighted IV reflects CrowdStrike's premium platform position offset by high starting multiple and execution risk. At $435/share, the stock prices in a scenario significantly beyond the base case.

valuation_commentary.summary: CrowdStrike's DCF intrinsic value of $127.63 (base), $188.44 (bull), and $76.95 (bear) reflects the profound disconnect between the company's exceptional operational momentum and its current $435/share market price (~$109B market cap). The market is pricing in a sustained growth trajectory well above even the bull case in this model. At 22x ARR and ~100x FY2026 non-GAAP FCF, CRWD is valued as a category-defining platform with a decade-long compounding runway. The DCF approach may undervalue a platform company with strong network effects and recurring revenue, but it clearly signals that the margin of safety is very thin - or negative - at current prices unless one assumes continuation of 20%+ FCF growth well beyond the 5-year projection window.
valuation_commentary.key_assumptions_sensitivity: The intrinsic value is highly sensitive to the terminal growth rate and WACC. Assuming 10% WACC and 3% terminal growth (base), IV is ~$128. If the market is 'right' and is effectively pricing in 5+ more years of 20%+ FCF growth before terminal deceleration, a 10-year DCF (not shown) would yield substantially higher values. Investors should consider whether CrowdStrike's $10B ARR vision (from $4.9B today) justifies the current price - if achieved by FY2029, and assuming 35% FCF margins at that scale, the implied FCF would be ~$3.5B, making the current enterprise value of ~$105B approximately 30x that FCF - still requiring a 3%+ terminal growth assumption and sub-10% WACC to be fair value.
valuation_commentary.outage_impact: The July 2024 outage creates a near-term FCF headwind (Customer Commitment Package credits) and a lingering Delta Airlines litigation risk ($500M+ claim). These risks are partially reflected in the bear case but represent tail risk not fully captured in the base case.
valuation_commentary.recommended_entry_zone: Value investors requiring a 15% annualized CAGR to terminal value would need to purchase at $69 (base) to $109 (bull) to achieve that return target. The current price of $435 implies the market expects a much longer high-growth runway or accepts a significantly lower required return.
